reasoning: The Acme Bank AI Governance Policy (ACME-POL-AIGOV-002, Section 5) requires a Pre-Deployment Risk Assessment that explicitly covers the system's intended purpose/use cases, known limitations, and fairness/bias considerations — which aligns partially with the Article 9(2)(b) obligation to estimate/evaluate risks arising from intended use. The Model Risk Management Standard (ACME-POL-MRM-003, Section 1) also indicates requirements to identify, assess, and manage model risk, supporting that risk estimation is within scope. However, the fragments do not explicitly require estimation and evaluation of risks under "reasonably foreseeable misuse," nor do they explicitly state the need to quantify/estimate or evaluate those risks (they describe topics to cover but not the required risk-estimation/evaluation activity, methods, or coverage of foreseeable misuse). Missing specifics that would be needed to map fully to Article 9(2)(b): an explicit obligation to assess risks from reasonably foreseeable misuse, explicit language on estimation/evaluation (vs. listing topics), required methods/metrics or depth of assessment, and whether this assessment is lifecycle/ongoing or limited to pre-deployment. A human Compliance Analyst should review and confirm whether the existing Pre-Deployment Risk Assessment and Model Risk Management Standard are interpreted/implemented to include explicit estimation and evaluation of risks from intended use and reasonably foreseeable misuse.

retrieved_fragments.excerpt:
Before any AI system is deployed to production, the owning business unit must
complete a Pre-Deployment Risk Assessment covering:

- Intended purpose and use cases
- Data sources and data quality
- Known limitations of the model or system
- Fairness and bias considerations
- Sign-off from the AIGC for high-impact systems

All AI systems must be registered in the Acme Bank AI System Inventory prior to
deployment, with the following minimum metadata: system name, business owner,
intended purpose, data sources, and deployment date.

retrieved_fragments.policy_title: Acme Bank Model Risk Management Standard
retrieved_fragments.excerpt:
This Standard sets out the requirements for identifying, assessing, and managing
model risk across all quantitative models used by Acme Bank, including statistical,
machine learning, and AI-based models.
